title: What a Model Refuses, a State Fears: Political Threat Models in Language-Model Guardrails

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model refusal rates on a factorial benchmark of political prompts that vary in collective-action potential (e.g., organizing a protest vs. writing a solo opinion piece) and political valence (pro-government vs. anti-government).

Using a counterfactual referent manipulation that holds the prompt text exactly identical while substituting only the target country (e.g., China vs. a foreign democracy vs. a fictional generic locale) to measure state-specific censorship.

Comparing native refusal rates and vulnerability to adversarial jailbreaks (porosity) across different testing languages (English, Chinese, French) to determine if models are more strictly guarded in their developer's home language.
